title: Ha ..., akkor ...: If This, Then That

sections.title: A simple if-then sentence
sections.content: ha means "if". For something realistic — not a wish or a hypothetical, just a plain fact about what happens when something else happens — Hungarian keeps the present tense on both sides of the sentence, exactly like the ha-clause and the main clause were separate statements: Ha késik a vonat, várunk ("If the train is late, we wait"). akkor ("then") is optional but common at the start of the second half, especially when the ha-clause comes first.

sections.title: ha and akkor
rows: Ha késik a vonat, akkor várunk.
If the train is late, then we wait.

items.spanish: Ha eltűnik a poggyászom, azonnal szólok valakinek.
items.english: If my luggage goes missing, I'll tell someone right away.

items.spanish: Ha nincs helyünk, akkor a következő vonattal megyünk.
items.english: If we don't have a seat, then we'll go on the next train.

sections.content: ha always starts its own clause, and a comma separates the two halves — Ha késik a vonat, várunk, never Késik a vonat ha, várunk.
